newsitem.title: USA: U.S. court upholds partial stay on FCC phone rules.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court upholds partial stay on FCC phone rules.

text.p: A U.S. court on Thursday put on hold key provisions of a landmark federal rule on bringing competition to local telephone markets while it considers a legal challenge to the measure.

"The pricing rules and the pick-and-choose rules are going to be stayed for the duration of the appeal," said Dana McWay, chief deputy clerk for the Eighth U.S. Circuit of Appeals. "The rest is no longer stayed."

The ruling appeared to represent a victory for GTE Corp, the Baby Bell companies and other local phone carriers that challenged the FCC order. They contended that the FCC exceeded its authority by imposing an "arbitrary" pricing system when it issued the complex interconnection order in August.
State regulators have also challenged the order, calling it an intrusion on their authority to set local telecommunications policy.
By contrast, the ruling could pose a setback for the FCC and long-distance carriers such as AT&T Corp who are trying to break into the local phone market.

"This is a significant setback for the FCC for two reasons. The court of appeals has concluded there is potential significant merit to the challenge to the pricing portions of the order. And second, this is going to slow down the implementation of local competition," said Alfred Mamlet, an attorney for Steptoe & Johnson in Washington.
In the decision released on Tuesday, the court said the stay was in the public interest, and that irreparable damage might be caused to some local phone companies if the stay were not granted.
"We believe the petitioners have adequately demonstrated that they will be irreparably harmed if a stay of the FCC's pricing rules is not granted," the court wrote.
The court also said the Telecommunications Act of 1996 authorized the state commissions -- not the FCC -- to enforce the act's requirements that rates be "just and reasonable."
